newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ulster farmers meet Dutch minister about BSE.
newsitem.headline: Ulster farmers meet Dutch minister about BSE.

text.p: The Ulster farmers union and the Northern Ireland Meat Exporters Association met the Dutch farm minister Jozias van Aartsen on Monday about easing the mad cow export ban on British beef.

"We are just having an informal meeting to get to know each other because the Netherlands is taking over the Presidency of the European Union from January 1 and will be dealing with the problem," Cecil Mather of the meat exporters' association said.

He aded that farmers organisations in Northern Ireland want the Dutch Presidency to focus on an early lifting of the export ban imposed on Britain by the European Union in March because of a health scare over Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).

Mather welcomed the announcement by British Agriculute Minister Douglas Hogg that an additional slaughter of 100,000 suspect cattle was being introduced but blamed "Westminister Politics" for the delaying the decision.
"The British government made an agreement at the Florence Summit and it should have been complied with much earlier.
"The delay has been due to internal politics at Westminster," he said.
The Deputy President of the Ulster Farmers' Union, Walter Elliott, said that he had an open mind on how the lifting of the ban should be implemented.
"Obviously it will have to be a U.K. wide arrangement but how various parts of the U.K. fit in remains to be discussed," he said. REUTER
